title: Handoff by constraint id: one vocabulary from ticket to test
summary: A designer writes a ticket whose acceptance criteria are constraint ids. The engineer's agent implements against them, QA reads the same ids in the test output, and the pull request cites them. Nobody re-explains the requirement.

persona.role: Product designer handing an agent-approval step to engineering
persona.context: Has a mockup of the approval step. Cannot read a JSON contract and should not have to. Past handoffs lost the keyboard and screen reader behavior between the mockup and the build.
persona.goal: Acceptance criteria that mean the same thing to the engineer, the agent, and QA, and that they can check themselves.

trigger: They open a ticket: "Approval before the agent sends drafted emails."

advantage.claim: The ticket, the code, the test, and the review all point at the same rule by name.
advantage.why_it_holds: Constraint ids are stable, each has a plain statement and a rationale, and the scaffolded tests are named for them. Figma's server carries the look of a design, not its behavior; spec-driven workflows invent a fresh vocabulary per project; guideline numbers do not appear in anyone's test output.

preconditions: The catalog's two MCP tools are callable (see RUNNER.md, Connecting the catalog).
A scratch project created with `npm init -y`, containing a tsconfig.json whose compilerOptions set "jsx": "react-jsx".

The ticket, as written by the designer: "Approval before the agent sends drafted emails. Done when it meets approval-gate: explicit-consent, accurate-preview, no-preselected-approve, irreversible-labeled, controls-accessible, gate-announced."

steps.action: Read what the pattern is for, in plain language, on its page.
steps.expect: The plain-language overview and the numbered constraints.

steps.action: Paste a link to each rule into the ticket, so anyone reading it lands on the rule itself.
steps.expect: The page scrolls to the explicit-consent constraint.

steps.action: As the engineer's agent: pull the look of the approval step from the design file.

uses.name: Figma MCP server (design context for the selected frame)

steps.expect: Layout, variables, and any mapped code components. Behavior comes from the contract, not from here.

steps.action: Scaffold the pattern named in the ticket.
Write the returned files into the project unmodified.

uses.change: Create one file per entry in the response's files array, with the returned content byte for byte.

steps.action: Install the verify dependencies and run the verify command.

uses.run: npm i -D <verify.dependencies, space separated> && cd src/patterns/approval-gate && <verify.command>

steps.action: As QA: for each id in the ticket, find the passing tests named for it.
steps.expect: Every ticket id maps to at least one passing test whose name starts with that id.

uses.change: The ticket's ids as a checklist, each with the test that proves it, then the contract version and hash.

steps.expect: A description the designer can tick off against their own ticket.

success.criterion: Every acceptance criterion in the ticket is a real rule.
success.check: Each id in the ticket appears in the constraints array returned in s4.
For each ticket id, the s6 output contains a passing test whose name starts with that id.

success.criterion: A non-engineer can open each criterion and read it.
success.check: Each link from s2 resolves and lands on the named constraint.

success.criterion: The pull request speaks the ticket's language.
success.check: PR-DESCRIPTION.md lists every ticket id with a test name and carries the version and full contract_hash.

gaps.summary: The site is not deployed, so no pattern page can be reached.
gaps.evidence: https://agent-ux-contracts.vercel.app returned Vercel DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND on 2026-11-11. The site builds cleanly from this repository.
gaps.fix: Reconnect or redeploy the Vercel project.

gaps.summary: A constraint cannot be linked to. The pattern page renders constraints as numbered clauses with no id on each.
gaps.evidence: site/app/patterns/[id]/page.tsx sets no id attribute on constraint elements.
gaps.fix: Render each constraint with its id as the element id, and show a copy-link control beside it.

automation.schedule: After the site is live, on every deploy, to check that each constraint link still resolves.
automation.notes: The runner plays the designer, the engineer's agent, and QA in turn. s1 and s2 are blocked until the site is deployed and anchors exist; the rest runs today.
